text:
Rachel Kim: We need to lock “reference readiness” criteria for the program. Goal: make it easy for AEs to request + not burn customers / create a million bespoke asks. Can we align today?

Miguel Santos: +1. Also want clarity on what “outcomes” we can collect passively vs what requires customer involvement. We’re already asking them for QBR prep.

Jasmine Liu: Please keep this lightweight. If it’s >30 min/month of customer time, it won’t scale. Also: we should have a path for “reference-call-only” vs “public case study.”

Markus Klein: From SE side: we need minimum technical bar before we put anyone in front of prospects. If their setup is still changing weekly, it’s risky.

Soojin Lee: Messaging/claims angle: we need validated metrics + measurement notes. I’m happy with “up to X%” style only if we can tie it to a specific window + workload description.

Rachel Kim: Draft strawman readiness rubric (tell me what’s too strict):
1) In production (or production-like) at least 30 days on Redwood, stable traffic.
2) Identified champion willing to do 2–3 reference calls/quarter (and knows what they can/can’t share).
3) Health is Green (no open Sev1/Sev2, no active escalations, renewal risk low).
4) Metrics are available in Console + we can reproduce/validate (latency p50/p95, error rate, throughput, cost/token or cost/query).
5) Internal approvals: AE + CSM sign off; SE confirms architecture isn’t “one-off”; Marketing + Legal only required for public case study.
(reactions: :thumbsup: x4)

Logan Wright: For #4 we can standardize: use Console dashboard export + a single “measurement window” (e.g., last 14 days) and “workload definition” (model version, context length range, streaming yes/no). We should avoid asking customers to screenshot stuff manually.

Sana Farid: Agree. Also we need baselines. If we can’t get “before Redwood” from their old stack, we can still do “current Redwood performance” but we should label it clearly (no implied delta). For deltas, require: (a) baseline source, (b) date range, (c) what changed.

Miguel Santos: On customer burden: my suggestion is we collect 80% internally:
- Latency/throughput/error: Console + our telemetry
- Usage/cost: Console token cost breakdown + billing exports
- Reliability/incident stats: Jira Support tags per customer + status page events
Customer only does:
- 30 min “story + context” interview
- Quote approval + boundaries (“don’t mention X”)
- Optional: review the diagram / architecture section

Simran Kaur: For architecture validation, we can do one 45 min technical validation call where we confirm: deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), routing/fallback policies, caching/batching/quantization settings (if relevant), and what parts are safe to publish. After that, we shouldn’t keep pinging.

Isabelle Laurent: For ops/CRM: we need fields that match the rubric so Sales can self-serve. Something like:
- Reference readiness: Not ready / Reference-call-only / Case study candidate / Approved-public
- Champion identified (Y/N)
- Last validated metrics date
- Allowed topics (multi-select)
- Disallowed topics (free text)
Then automation: if “Approved-public” and last validated metrics >45 days old -> reminder to CSM.

Tyler Benson: +1 and please keep it consistent with the intake form. I can build the form so AEs don’t Slack random asks. Minimum fields: prospect name, stage, what objection they’re trying to address, target date, requested deployment mode story.

Rachel Kim: Good call. We should also define SLAs:
- CSM response to reference request: 1 business day
- If approved: schedule within 5 business days (customer availability dependent)
- Limit: max 2 reference calls/month per customer unless explicitly opted in
(reactions: :eyes: x2)

Jasmine Liu: Add guardrail: we don’t put customers on calls if they’re in an unresolved incident with us, even if “minor.” Trust > pipeline.

Markus Klein: For SE attendance: reference calls should not always require SE. But for first call with a customer, I’d prefer an SE shadowing to ensure technical questions don’t go sideways.

Miguel Santos: Maybe rule:
- First reference call = CSM + optional SE (based on complexity)
- Subsequent calls = CSM only, unless prospect is deep technical evaluation

Soojin Lee: On “allowed/disallowed”: we should give customers a simple menu so they don’t have to invent policy language. Examples:
Allowed topics: latency improvements, cost controls (batching/caching), deployment mode (VPC/on-prem in general terms), observability, rollouts/fallback.
Not allowed: specific cloud region, exact traffic volumes, vendor comparisons by name (unless they approve), internal compliance details.

Sana Farid: Also standard metric phrasing:
- Always include window (e.g., “p95 over a 14-day period”)
- Include workload characteristics (“streaming chat, median prompt ~1.2k tokens”) if we publish numbers
- Avoid “guarantees” unless tied to contract/SLA language

Logan Wright: Re: incident stats, easiest is for us to produce: “Sev1/Sev2 incidents in last 90 days attributable to Redwood” + “mitigation steps.” We can pull from Jira + incident labels. Customers shouldn’t be asked to remember outages.

Rachel Kim: Proposal: reference readiness tiers
Tier A (Reference-call-ready): meets 1–3 + has boundaries + internal signoff. Metrics optional.
Tier B (Case-study-ready internal): meets Tier A + metrics validated + architecture validated.
Tier C (Public-approved): Tier B + signed quote/logo release + customer final approval.

Isabelle Laurent: Works for CRM. We can map Tier A/B/C to dropdown values.

Tyler Benson: Can we define what “metrics validated” means? Otherwise it’s subjective.

Simran Kaur: Definition suggestion:
- SE confirms request routing/config + model versions used match what’s in the write-up
- Logan provides Console export (latency/cost/errors) and stores in shared folder
- Sana signs off on calculation notes (baseline vs current, denominators)
- CSM confirms customer agrees the numbers are representative (they can say “yes these are in line with what we see”) — no extra analysis needed from them

Miguel Santos: That last part (“representative”) is key. We can do it as a single yes/no email with a pasted summary table.

Soojin Lee: + we should keep a “claims register” per customer: exact numbers + approved phrasing + expiration date.

Jasmine Liu: Action items:
1) Rachel to publish the rubric + tiers in the CS playbook (draft by EOW).
2) Isabelle/Tyler to align on HubSpot fields + intake form routing.
3) Logan/Sana to provide a 1-page “metrics validation notes” template.
4) Markus/Simran to define when SE attends and the technical validation checklist.

Rachel Kim: I’ll draft and share in this channel for async comments. Please reply with anything that would make this unworkable for your teams.
(reactions: :thumbsup: x6)

Slackbot: Reminder set by Rachel Kim to review “reference readiness rubric” in 3 days.
